checklist.step: Extract the internal producer roster as of quarter end
actions: In the agency/producer management system run the Producer Roster export with Status = Active as of the last calendar day of the quarter.
Include columns: producer name, NPN, resident state, license number, appointed states, appointment effective dates, contract status and termination date.
Ask the Distribution Operations Manager to confirm no producers were onboarded outside the system during the quarter and file the written reply.
Save the export as roster-<yyyy>Q<n>.xlsx in the reconciliation folder.
checklist.done: a dated quarter-end roster export with NPN and appointment columns sits in the reconciliation folder with Distribution's completeness confirmation.

checklist.step: Pull the state appointment record from the NIPR Producer Database
actions: Log in to NIPR Gateway with the company account and open Products ▸ PDB Reports.
Run a Company Appointment report for each writing company NAIC co-code, all states, as of the quarter-end date.
Download the CSV with producer NPN, state, line of authority, appointment status and effective/termination dates.
Spot-open five producers in PDB Producer Lookup and compare their detail screens to the CSV to confirm the report populated correctly.
checklist.done: a quarter-end NIPR appointment CSV per NAIC co-code is saved and spot-checked against PDB detail screens.

checklist.step: Capture the BMA register position for Bermuda intermediaries
actions: Open the BMA website Supervision & Regulation ▸ Register of Insurance Intermediaries and locate every broker, agent and salesman the roster shows as Bermuda-facing.
Print each register entry to PDF, named bma-register-<intermediary>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf, capturing registered name, class and registration date.
For any roster intermediary absent from the register, note the row as a potential s.10 breach for the exception log.
Confirm with the Corporate Secretary that no intermediary particulars (name, address, class) changed in the quarter without a BMA notification.
checklist.done: every Bermuda-facing intermediary has a dated register capture or is flagged as an exception, and particular changes are confirmed notified.

checklist.step: Build the three-way match workbook
actions: In Excel load the roster export, the NIPR CSVs and the BMA register list onto separate sheets.
Key the match on NPN + state for US producers and on registered name for Bermuda intermediaries, using exact-match lookups — no fuzzy matching.
Add a Status column per row: MATCHED, ROSTER-ONLY (active producer, no appointment), NIPR-ONLY (appointment, no active producer), or DATA-MISMATCH (name/license discrepancies).
Freeze the workbook as recon-<yyyy>Q<n>.xlsx before any remediation edits so the pre-remediation position is preserved.
checklist.done: every roster and NIPR row carries exactly one match status in a frozen pre-remediation workbook.

checklist.step: Investigate every ROSTER-ONLY producer for unauthorized business
actions: For each ROSTER-ONLY row, query the billing/commission platform for new-business commission credited to that NPN in the affected state during the quarter.
Where commission exists, pull the underlying policy numbers and first-application dates from the policy administration system.
Compare each first-application date to the state's just-in-time appointment window (commonly 15 days from first application) to decide whether the window was already blown.
Mark rows with business written as UNAUTHORIZED-BUSINESS exceptions and rows without business as APPOINTMENT-GAP-ONLY.
checklist.done: every ROSTER-ONLY row is classified as unauthorized business or gap-only, with policy numbers and day counts recorded.

checklist.step: Investigate every NIPR-ONLY appointment for missed terminations
actions: For each NIPR-ONLY row, pull the producer's contract termination date from the agency/producer management system.
Compute days elapsed = quarter-end date − contract termination date and flag every row over 30 days as a late-termination exception.
Ask the Agency Relations Manager in writing whether any NIPR-ONLY producer is a pending rehire that should keep its appointment; file the reply.
List the confirmed-dead appointments for termination filing, noting each state's termination fee treatment.
checklist.done: every NIPR-ONLY appointment is either justified in writing or queued for termination with its elapsed-day count.

checklist.step: Verify license status and lines of authority for the active roster
actions: In NIPR PDB run a license-status report for all MATCHED producers and read license status, expiration date and lines of authority.
Flag any license expiring inside the next quarter and any producer whose line of authority does not cover the product they are selling (e.g. annuity sales on a life-only line).
Cross-check flagged producers against the product mix recorded in the CRM.
Add license-expiry and LOA mismatches to the exception list with the producing state and expiry date.
checklist.done: license status and lines of authority are verified for every matched producer and mismatches are on the exception list.

checklist.step: File missing appointments through NIPR Gateway
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Products ▸ Appointments, select the writing company NAIC co-code and enter each gap producer's NPN and state.
Select the correct line of authority and submit, paying the state appointment fee through the NIPR billing account.
Download the NIPR transaction confirmation PDF for each submission and attach it to the workbook row.
For states not supporting NIPR electronic appointment, prepare the state's own appointment form and record the mailing/portal submission date.
checklist.done: every appointment gap has a NIPR confirmation (or state-form submission record) attached to its workbook row.

checklist.step: File appointment terminations within the 30-day rule
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Products ▸ Terminations and file termination for each confirmed-dead appointment, entering the contract termination date as the effective date.
Where the termination is for cause, coordinate with Regulatory Counsel on the state's for-cause disclosure attachment before submitting.
Download each termination confirmation and attach it to the workbook row.
Diary the next contract-termination feed so future terminations are filed inside 30 days rather than caught at quarter end.
checklist.done: all dead appointments are terminated in NIPR with confirmations attached and for-cause disclosures cleared by counsel.

checklist.step: Notify the BMA of Bermuda intermediary changes within 14 days
actions: For any change in a Bermuda-registered intermediary's particulars or any new/ceased intermediary relationship, draft the written notification to the BMA referencing Insurance Act 1978 s.10.
Have the Principal Representative review the draft, then submit it through the BMA's electronic submission channel or by letter to the Authority.
Count days from the triggering event to submission and record the count on the workbook row — the window is 14 days.
File the stamped/acknowledged copy in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: every intermediary change carries a BMA notification submitted within 14 days, with the acknowledgement filed.

checklist.step: Reconcile appointment-renewal invoices against the live appointment set
actions: Pull the quarter's state appointment-renewal invoices from the NIPR billing account and any direct state invoices from Accounts Payable.
Match invoiced appointments to the post-remediation appointment set; renewals invoiced for terminated producers indicate terminations filed late or not at all.
Hand the list of wrongly invoiced renewals to the Accounts Payable Specialist with instructions to dispute rather than pay.
Record the annualized fee leakage from stale appointments in the reconciliation report.
checklist.done: renewal invoices reconcile to live appointments and wrongly invoiced renewals are in dispute, with fee leakage quantified.

checklist.step: Place commission holds on producers pending appointment cure
actions: In the billing/commission platform set a commission hold flag on every producer with an open UNAUTHORIZED-BUSINESS exception.
Notify the Commission Analyst and the producer's Agency Relations Manager of the hold and the cure condition (appointment confirmation on file).
Release each hold only after the NIPR confirmation is attached to the workbook row and the Producer Compliance Manager initials the release.
Record hold and release dates on the exception row.
checklist.done: every unauthorized-business producer is on commission hold, and no hold is released without an appointment confirmation and an initialed release.

checklist.step: Log all exceptions with root cause and disposition
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with producer NPN, state, exception class, policy numbers where business was written, and the day-count math.
Assign a root cause: onboarding bypassed licensing, termination feed missed, state rule change, or data-entry error.
For unauthorized business, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel covering the affected states' voluntary-disclosure rules.
Set a remediation owner and date on every issue before the report is finalized.
checklist.done: each exception is a tracker issue with root cause, owner, date and — for unauthorized business — a counsel-led self-report assessment.

checklist.step: Compile and sign the quarterly reconciliation report
actions: Assemble the report: population counts per source, match rates, exception counts by class, remediation status, fee leakage and the BMA notification log.
Compare this quarter's exception rate to the prior four quarters and comment on the trend.
Sign and date the report as Producer Compliance Manager and obtain the Head of Distribution's acknowledgement of any producer-behavior findings.
Deliver the signed report to the Head of Compliance by the 20th of the month following quarter end.
checklist.done: a signed, trend-commented reconciliation report is with the Head of Compliance by the 20th.

checklist.step: File the reconciliation evidence pack for retention
actions: Upload to the compliance evidence repository: the frozen pre-remediation workbook, the roster and NIPR extracts, BMA register captures, NIPR confirmations, the exception log export and the signed report.
Index the pack under REG-057-C25 / <yyyy>Q<n> and apply the 7-year retention label.
Run a retrieval check: search the repository by one sampled producer NPN and confirm the pack surfaces.
Record the repository link on the compliance calendar entry to close the quarter's task.
checklist.done: the complete evidence pack is filed under REG-057-C25 with 7-year retention and passes a retrieval check.

testing.step: Build the tested population from commission and appointment activity
actions: Extract from the billing/commission platform every producer NPN credited with new-business commission in the test year, by writing company and state.
Extract from NIPR Gateway the year's appointment and termination transaction log for each NAIC co-code.
Union the two lists with the quarter-end rosters so producers appearing in any source are in the population.
Record row counts per source and the extraction dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: a unioned population of commission-earning and appointment-transacting producers exists with documented counts and dates.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the general ledger commission expense
actions: Pull the year's commission expense balance from the general ledger commission accounts.
Tie the billing/commission platform extract total to the GL balance within 1%, listing reconciling items (accruals, clawbacks) explicitly.
Resolve any residual difference with the Controller before sampling — an unreconciled population invalidates the test.
Document the tie-out in the workpaper.
testing.done: the commission population ties to the GL within 1% with reconciling items itemized and signed off.

testing.step: Draw the sample and fix the selection method
actions: Select 100% of producers flagged as UNAUTHORIZED-BUSINESS in any quarterly reconciliation during the year.
Add 25 producers drawn at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population, minimum 40 in total.
Include at least one Bermuda-registered intermediary and at least one for-cause termination if any exist.
Record seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all unauthorized-business rows, a Bermuda intermediary and a for-cause termination is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the PDB appointment lookup for every sampled producer
actions: In NIPR PDB look up each sampled NPN and read appointment status, effective date and line of authority for each state the producer wrote in.
Reach your own appointed/not-appointed conclusion before opening the reconciliation workbook.
Compare to the workbook's match status; any difference — including right conclusion from wrong data — is an exception.
Screenshot each PDB detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled producer has an independent PDB re-performance note and captured screen.

testing.step: Trace sampled business to appointments that pre-date it
actions: For each sampled producer, pull the first-application date of each policy written per state from the policy administration system.
Compare the first-application date to the PDB appointment effective date and the state's JIT window.
List every policy written before appointment (outside the JIT window) as a confirmed unauthorized-business instance.
Cross-check that each confirmed instance already appears in the quarterly exception log — absence from the log is a second, separate exception.
testing.done: every sampled policy traces to a timely appointment or is a documented exception, and log completeness is verified.

testing.step: Recompute termination and BMA notification day counts
actions: For sampled terminations, recompute NIPR filing date − contract termination date and compare to the 30-day rule.
For sampled Bermuda intermediary changes, recompute BMA submission date − triggering event date against the 14-day window in Insurance Act 1978 s.10.
Verify each date against source documents (contract termination letters, BMA acknowledgements), not against the workbook.
List every blown window with its actual day count.
testing.done: all sampled day counts are independently recomputed from source documents with breaches listed.

testing.step: Verify each quarter's reconciliation ran, was signed and was timely
actions: Open the compliance evidence repository index for REG-057-C25 and confirm four quarterly packs exist for the year.
Check each pack contains the frozen pre-remediation workbook, source extracts and a report signed by the Producer Compliance Manager.
Compare each report's delivery date to the 20th-of-following-month deadline.
Note any quarter run late, unsigned or with a missing artifact as an exception.
testing.done: four complete, signed, timely quarterly packs are verified in the repository or gaps are listed.

testing.step: Test commission holds on unauthorized-business producers
actions: For each unauthorized-business producer in the sample, read the hold flag history in the billing/commission platform.
Confirm the hold was set within 5 business days of the exception being raised and released only after the NIPR confirmation date.
Query commission payments during the hold window; any payment that leaked through is an exception.
Attach the hold-history extract to the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled hold was timely, effective and released only on cure, or leakage is documented.

testing.step: Log test exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per test exception, distinguishing control failures (reconciliation missed it) from compliance breaches (unauthorized business, blown windows).
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date.
For any breach not previously self-assessed, route to Regulatory Counsel for a disclosure decision covering the affected states and the BMA.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, date and — where new — a counsel disclosure decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-unauthorized-business and ≤2% administrative thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references.
Have the Chief Audit Executive, who processed no sampled transaction, review and sign the workpaper.
Report the result to the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C25.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

In-scope systems.value: Conduct procedure library in the document management repository (versioned, approval-workflow enabled); training completions in the learning management system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Conduct Procedure Governance Standard — inventory of required procedures mapped Code-paragraph-by-paragraph, owner per document, annual review cadence, version control and approval workflow

Compliance procedure approved.value: Each conduct procedure approved by its business owner and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager; the governance standard itself approved by the Head of Compliance annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Every procedure carries a next-review date no more than 12 months out; the s.8A Declaration of Compliance (which attests Code observance) is filed with the statutory financial return within 4 months of financial year end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Document management repository review-date alerts fire to each procedure owner at T-60/T-30/T-7 days; an overdue list goes to the Head of Compliance monthly

checklist.step: Refresh the Code-to-procedure mapping matrix
actions: Download the current BMA Insurance Code of Conduct from bma.bm ▸ Legislation & Guidance and diff it against last year's saved copy paragraph by paragraph.
In the mapping matrix list every Code paragraph imposing a conduct obligation and the procedure document(s) that implement it, by document id.
Mark paragraphs with no implementing procedure as GAP rows and paragraphs whose procedure predates a Code change as STALE rows.
Date-stamp the refreshed matrix and file it in the document management repository.
checklist.done: a dated matrix maps every Code paragraph to a procedure, with GAP and STALE rows explicitly flagged.

checklist.step: Inventory the conduct procedure library and its metadata
actions: In the document management repository run a metadata export of the conduct library: document id, title, owner, version, approval date, last review date, next review date.
Flag every document with next review date in the past, a vacant owner (leaver), or approval workflow incomplete.
Reconcile the export against the mapping matrix so no matrix-referenced document is missing from the library.
Send each flagged owner a written review assignment with a due date inside 30 days.
checklist.done: the library export reconciles to the matrix and every overdue or ownerless document has an assigned reviewer and due date.

checklist.step: Draft procedures for uncovered conduct areas
actions: For each GAP row, name a business drafting owner (e.g. Complaints Manager for complaint handling, Claims Director / Manager for claims settlement conduct) and issue a drafting brief quoting the Code paragraph verbatim.
Require each draft to state: the obligation, the operational steps, the responsible roles, the records produced and where they are filed.
Set drafting deadlines that land all gaps closed at least 30 days before the s.8A declaration date.
Track drafting progress weekly on the matrix.
checklist.done: every GAP row has a named drafter, a brief quoting the Code text and a deadline inside the declaration runway.

checklist.step: Run the annual substantive review of each existing procedure
actions: For each in-date procedure, have the document owner re-read it against the current Code paragraph and against how the process actually runs today.
Require the owner to interview at least one front-line performer (e.g. a Contact Center Supervisor for complaint intake) and note any divergence between the written and actual process.
Record the review outcome on the document: reaffirmed unchanged, amended, or withdrawn-and-replaced, with the reviewer's name and date.
Route amended documents back through the repository approval workflow.
checklist.done: every procedure carries a current-year review outcome grounded in a front-line check, with amendments routed for approval.

checklist.step: Verify complaint-handling procedure meets the Code's specific tests
actions: Check the complaints procedure defines a complaint, sets acknowledgement and resolution timeframes, and names the escalation path to the Complaints Manager.
Confirm the procedure requires a complaints register with root-cause coding and quarterly trend reporting to Market Conduct Compliance.
Confirm customers are told how to complain in policy documents and on the customer self-service portal, and that the wording matches the procedure.
Fix any mismatch between the register fields in the workflow/case management tool and the fields the procedure promises.
checklist.done: the complaints procedure, the register configuration and the customer-facing wording all agree and meet the Code's complaint-handling requirements.

checklist.step: Verify claims-conduct procedure covers fair and timely settlement
actions: Check the claims-conduct procedure states acknowledgement, investigation and payment timeframe standards and the interim-payment rule for long-tail claims.
Confirm denial letters must cite the policy provision relied on and state the complaint/appeal route, and spot-open three recent denial letters in the Claims Platform to confirm practice matches.
Confirm reservation-of-rights wording and unrepresented-claimant safeguards are documented.
Log any letter template in the Claims Platform that diverges from the procedure as a remediation item.
checklist.done: the claims procedure covers timeframes, denial content and safeguards, and sampled live letters match it.

checklist.step: Verify sales and disclosure procedures for marketing conduct
actions: Check the marketing-review procedure requires pre-use compliance sign-off of every customer-facing advertisement and illustration, with a review log.
Confirm product disclosure procedures require clear statement of coverage, exclusions, charges and cancellation rights before sale.
Sample three advertisements released this year from the marketing automation platform and confirm each has a logged pre-use sign-off.
Record any unreviewed release as an exception with the release date and channel.
checklist.done: marketing and disclosure procedures require pre-use sign-off and sampled releases each show one.

checklist.step: Approve every new or amended procedure through the workflow
actions: Route each new or amended procedure through the repository approval workflow: business owner approval, then Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager, then Head of Compliance for Code-significant documents.
Reject any document lacking a Code-paragraph reference in its header or lacking a named operational owner.
On approval, set version number, approval date and next review date (≤12 months) in the document metadata.
Publish the approved version and archive the superseded version with its full history.
checklist.done: all new and amended procedures are workflow-approved with version, approval date and a ≤12-month next-review date set.

checklist.step: Communicate changes and retire superseded guidance
actions: Publish a change notice to affected teams naming each amended procedure, what changed and the effective date.
Search shared drives and team wikis for superseded copies and replace them with links to the repository version.
Ask each affected team lead to confirm in writing that local work instructions were updated.
File the change notices and confirmations with the review records.
checklist.done: change notices are issued, stray superseded copies are replaced with links, and team confirmations are on file.

checklist.step: Train affected staff on materially changed procedures
actions: For each materially changed procedure, build or update the training module in the learning management system and assign it to the affected role population.
Set a completion deadline of 30 days from assignment and enable automatic reminders at T-14 and T-3 days.
Pull the completion report at deadline and chase non-completers through their line managers.
File the completion report as conduct-training evidence for the year.
checklist.done: training on each material change is assigned, completed ≥95% by deadline, and the completion report is filed.

checklist.step: Test that day-to-day practice follows the written procedures
actions: Pick three conduct areas (rotating yearly) and walk through five live cases in each against the written procedure step by step.
For complaints, check acknowledgement and resolution dates in the workflow/case management tool against the procedure's timeframes.
Record each divergence as either a procedure defect (procedure wrong) or a practice defect (procedure ignored) — the fix differs.
Feed procedure defects back into the review cycle and practice defects to the area's manager for corrective action.
checklist.done: fifteen live cases across three areas are walked through, with each divergence classified and routed.

checklist.step: Log and remediate procedure gaps and overdue reviews
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every GAP row still open, every review overdue past its due date and every practice defect from the walkthroughs.
Assign root cause (new Code text, owner departure, process drift) and a named owner with a remediation date.
Review the open list monthly with the Head of Compliance until empty.
Close issues only when the repository shows the approved document or the corrected practice evidence.
checklist.done: every gap, overdue review and practice defect is a tracked issue closed only on documented cure.

checklist.step: Certify annual review completion for the s.8A declaration
actions: Assemble the completion certificate: matrix coverage (100% of Code paragraphs), count of procedures reviewed/amended/added, open exceptions and their dates.

Confirm no open exception is severe enough to qualify the Declaration of Compliance; where one is, brief Regulatory Counsel and the Principal Representative on the wording implications before the declaration is signed.
Sign the certificate and deliver it to the Corporate Secretary as backing evidence for the s.8A declaration filed with the statutory financial return.
Diary next year's review cycle start 9 months ahead of the next declaration date.
checklist.done: a signed completion certificate backs the s.8A declaration, with any qualifying issue escalated before signature.

checklist.step: Brief the board committee on conduct-procedure health
actions: Prepare a one-page conduct-procedure health summary: coverage, overdue counts, walkthrough findings and remediation status.
Upload it to the board portal for the next Risk/Compliance Committee meeting pack.
Present the summary and record the committee's challenge and any directed actions in the minutes.
Track directed actions in the tracker with the committee date as the source reference.
checklist.done: the committee has seen and minuted the conduct-procedure health summary and directed actions are tracked.

checklist.step: Archive the annual review evidence pack
actions: Upload the mapping matrix, library export, review records, approvals, training completion report, walkthrough notes and the signed completion certificate to the compliance evidence repository.
Index the pack under REG-057-C26 / <yyyy> and apply the 7-year retention label.
Run a retrieval check by searching for one amended procedure's prior version and confirming it surfaces with its approval history.
Link the pack on the compliance calendar entry to close the annual task.
checklist.done: the complete annual pack is filed with 7-year retention and prior versions are retrievable with history.

testing.step: Build the procedure population from the repository, not the matrix
actions: Independently export the conduct library metadata from the document management repository as of the test date.
Separately list every obligation-bearing paragraph of the current BMA Insurance Code of Conduct from the bma.bm text — without reference to Compliance's matrix.
Use the repository export as the tested population and your own Code paragraph list as the completeness benchmark.
Record both counts and extraction dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: an auditor-built Code paragraph list and a repository export exist independently of the control owner's matrix.

testing.step: Reconcile the auditor's Code list to the mapping matrix
actions: Compare your paragraph list to the matrix line by line and list paragraphs the matrix omits or maps to withdrawn documents.
Verify the matrix was refreshed against the current Code version by checking the Code version date it cites.
Treat every omitted paragraph as a coverage exception regardless of materiality.
Document the reconciliation in the workpaper.
testing.done: matrix completeness is independently verified with omissions listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw the procedure sample
actions: Select 100% of procedures added or materially amended in the year, plus a seeded random 10 of the remaining library, minimum 15 documents.
Ensure the sample spans at least four conduct areas including complaints and claims settlement.
Record seed, population size and selection date for re-drawability.
Pull each sampled document's full version history from the repository.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of ≥15 documents across ≥4 conduct areas is drawn with version histories pulled.

testing.step: Re-perform the Code conformity read on each sampled procedure
actions: Read each sampled procedure against its cited Code paragraph and reach your own conforms/does-not-conform conclusion before reading the owner's review record.
Check the procedure names responsible roles, operational steps and the records produced — a restatement of the Code with no operational content is a fail.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded review outcome; differences are exceptions.
Note your conclusion and reasoning per document in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled procedure has an independent conformity conclusion compared against the owner's review outcome.

testing.step: Verify review dates, approvals and version control on the sample
actions: For each sampled document read the repository audit trail: who approved, in what order, and on what dates.
Confirm the last review date is within 12 months and the approval chain matches the governance standard (owner → Market Conduct → Head of Compliance where required).
Confirm the superseded version is archived and retrievable, not overwritten.
Flag any approval done by the document's own author as a segregation exception.
testing.done: review recency, approval chains and version archival are verified from the audit trail for every sampled document.

testing.step: Trace training on materially changed procedures
actions: For each materially amended sampled procedure, pull the learning management system completion report for the assigned population.
Recompute the completion percentage at the 30-day deadline and compare to the ≥95% standard.
Cross-check five completers against HR records to confirm they hold roles the procedure actually affects.
List under-completion or misassigned populations as exceptions.
testing.done: training completion is independently recomputed for every material change with misassignments listed.

testing.step: Re-perform practice walkthroughs on two conduct areas
actions: Pick two conduct areas not covered by Compliance's own walkthroughs this year and pull five live cases each from the workflow/case management tool.
Step each case against the written procedure, checking dates, letters and approvals against the procedure's stated standards.
Independently confirm complaint acknowledgement/resolution timeframes by reading case timestamps, not summary reports.
Record divergences and classify each as procedure defect or practice defect.
testing.done: ten live cases across two fresh areas are independently walked through with divergences classified.

testing.step: Verify the s.8A declaration was supportably signed
actions: Obtain the signed Declaration of Compliance filed with the statutory financial return and the Head of Compliance completion certificate behind it.
Check the certificate date precedes the declaration signature date and that open exceptions at signature date were assessed for declaration impact in writing.
Confirm the declaration was filed within the statutory financial return deadline (4 months after financial year end).
Treat a declaration signed while an unassessed material gap was open as a reportable finding.
testing.done: the declaration is traced to a pre-dated completion certificate and a written exception assessment, filed on time.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception, splitting coverage gaps, conformity failures, stale reviews, training shortfalls and practice defects.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date for each.
Route any exception touching the signed s.8A declaration to Regulatory Counsel for a disclosure assessment.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception is tracked with root cause, owner and date, and declaration-touching items have a counsel assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute results against the 100%-coverage and zero-overdue thresholds and write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references.
Have the Chief Audit Executive, who authored no sampled procedure, review and sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Risk/Compliance Committee alongside the conduct-procedure health summary.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C26.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Scope the filing obligation by state and line against the participation threshold
actions: Pull prior-year direct written premium by state and MCAS line of business from the annual statement state pages in the statutory reporting system.
Compare each state/line premium to the $50,000 MCAS participation threshold and list every combination that must file.
Check the NAIC MCAS pages for lines newly added to MCAS this data year and for states newly participating.
Record the scoping worksheet with premium figures, thresholds and the in/out call per state/line, dated and initialed.
checklist.done: a dated scoping worksheet lists every in-scope state/line with the premium figure behind each call.

checklist.step: Confirm MCAS registration and user access in iSite+
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ and open the MCAS application; confirm each writing company's cocode appears with the correct lines registered.
Verify the MCAS Contact and the Attestor named in the application are current employees; update via the MCAS admin screen if either has left.
Confirm at least two staff hold working credentials so a single absence cannot block the filing.
Screenshot the registration screen into the cycle folder.
checklist.done: registration, contacts and dual credentials are confirmed in iSite+ with a dated screenshot.

checklist.step: Refresh the data-element mapping against the current Data Call & Definitions
actions: Download the current-year MCAS Data Call & Definitions for each in-scope line from the NAIC MCAS page.
Diff the definitions against last year's mapping book and mark every changed or added element (e.g. claim closed-without-payment definitions, lawsuit counts, digital-claims elements).
Update the mapping book so each MCAS element maps to a named field or derivation in the enterprise data warehouse.
Have the Data Quality Analyst countersign mappings that changed.
checklist.done: the mapping book reflects the current definitions with every change countersigned.

checklist.step: Extract source data from claims, policy and complaints systems
actions: Run the MCAS extract jobs in the enterprise data warehouse for the data year: claims opened/closed/paid by state and line from the Claims Platform feed, policies issued/cancelled/nonrenewed from the policy administration feed, and complaints from the complaints register.
Apply the mapping book's element definitions — e.g. count claims closed without payment per the MCAS definition, not the internal one.
Produce one dataset per state/line in the MCAS upload layout.
Log job run ids, row counts and extract dates in the cycle folder.
checklist.done: per-state/line datasets in upload layout exist with logged run ids and row counts.

checklist.step: Reconcile extract totals to the source systems of record
actions: Tie total claim counts per state to a direct Claims Platform query and policy counts to the policy administration system, tolerance zero.
Tie premium-related fields to the filed annual statement state pages.
Investigate every difference to a named cause (timing, mapping, duplicate feed) and correct the extract, never the reconciliation.
File the signed reconciliation with the datasets.
checklist.done: extract totals tie to claims, policy and annual-statement sources at zero tolerance with a signed reconciliation.

checklist.step: Run reasonableness and ratio checks before upload
actions: Compute the key MCAS ratios per state (claims closed without payment %, median days to final payment, lawsuit ratio, nonrenewal rate) in the validation workbook.
Compare each ratio to last year's submission and to the NAIC published industry medians; flag movements over 20% for written explanation.
Have the Claims Director / Manager confirm in writing any real operational cause behind a flagged movement.
Retain the ratio workbook as the pre-submission validation package.
checklist.done: every flagged ratio movement carries a written operational explanation in the validation package.

checklist.step: Load and validate each state dataset in the MCAS application
actions: In iSite+ open the MCAS application, select the company cocode, data year and line, and upload each state dataset or key it into the online form.
Run the application's embedded validations and clear every error; for warnings, enter the explanation the validation screen requests.
Complete the interrogatories section, answering from the mapping book rather than memory.
Save each state as validated-not-yet-attested and note its status in the tracking sheet.
checklist.done: every in-scope state/line sits in validated status with errors cleared and interrogatories answered.

checklist.step: Obtain attestation and submit before April 30
actions: Review the validation package and the per-state statuses, then have the registered Attestor complete the MCAS attestation in iSite+ for each company.
Submit every state/line and download the submission confirmation showing date, time and data year.
Verify each submission timestamp is on or before April 30 and record it in the tracking sheet.
Store all confirmations in the cycle folder the same day.
checklist.done: all in-scope filings show attested, submitted-on-time confirmations stored in the cycle folder.

checklist.step: Coordinate the Bermuda statutory financial return so both calendars hold
actions: Confirm with the Controller the Bermuda entity's statutory financial return (s.17–s.18) is on track for filing with the BMA within 4 months of financial year end, since MCAS and SFR share finance data-cut resources.
Align the data-cut dates so the MCAS extract does not conflict with the SFR close calendar; record the agreed dates.
Flag any resource clash to the Chief Financial Officer at least 60 days before the earlier deadline.
Note the SFR filing confirmation reference in the cycle folder once filed.
checklist.done: MCAS and SFR calendars are aligned in writing and both filings show on-time confirmations.

checklist.step: Answer post-submission state data-quality queries
actions: Monitor the MCAS contact mailbox and iSite+ messages for state analyst queries after the window closes.
For each query, re-derive the questioned element from the retained extract and reply within the state's requested turnaround, copying the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
Where the query exposes a data error, prepare a corrected dataset and resubmit through the MCAS application, logging the resubmission as an exception.
File all query correspondence with the cycle evidence.
checklist.done: every state query is answered on time from retained evidence, and any resubmission is logged as an exception.

checklist.step: Monitor MCAS-derived scrutiny signals
actions: After publication, compare the company's MCAS ratios to the NAIC industry results for each state and line.
Identify outlier positions likely to draw analyst attention (e.g. top-decile claims closed without payment) and open a pre-emptive internal review of each.
Brief the Chief Claims Officer on claims-driven outliers with the underlying case data.
Record outliers and review outcomes in the conduct-metrics file feeding REG-057-C28.
checklist.done: outlier ratios are identified, internally reviewed and handed to the conduct-metrics monitoring cycle.

checklist.step: Log cycle exceptions with root cause and disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any missed state, late submission, cleared-late validation error, resubmission or scoping miss found during the cycle.
Assign root cause (threshold mis-scoped, mapping stale, extract defect, resourcing) and a named owner with a remediation date.
For a late or missed filing, have Regulatory Counsel assess the state's penalty exposure and whether proactive contact with the state MCAS analyst is warranted.
Review open issues at the monthly reporting-governance meeting until closed.
checklist.done: every cycle exception is tracked with root cause, owner, date and a counsel penalty assessment where filings slipped.

checklist.step: Update the procedure and mapping book with lessons learned
actions: Hold a post-cycle review within 30 days of April 30 covering validation failures, query themes and effort bottlenecks.
Write the agreed changes into the MCAS Filing Procedure and the mapping book as next-cycle updates.
Route the updated procedure through document approval by the Statutory Reporting Manager.
Diary the next cycle kickoff for early January.
checklist.done: post-cycle changes are approved into the procedure and mapping book and the next kickoff is diarized.

checklist.step: Report cycle completion to compliance governance
actions: Summarize for the Head of Compliance: states filed, timeliness, validation statistics, resubmissions, outlier ratios and open exceptions.
Confirm in the summary that submission confirmations for 100% of in-scope filings are on file.
Present the summary at the compliance governance meeting and minute any directed actions.
Track directed actions in the tracker to closure.
checklist.done: a completion summary confirming 100% confirmations on file is minuted at compliance governance.

checklist.step: Archive the full cycle evidence pack
actions: Upload the scoping worksheet, mapping book, extracts and reconciliations, validation package, submission confirmations, query correspondence and exception log to the compliance evidence repository.
Index under REG-057-C27 / data year <yyyy> with the 7-year retention label.
Run a retrieval check by pulling one state's confirmation from the index.
Close the compliance calendar task with the repository link.
checklist.done: the cycle pack is filed with 7-year retention and passes a per-state retrieval check.

testing.step: Independently rebuild the in-scope filing population
actions: From the filed annual statement state pages, independently compute direct written premium by state and MCAS line for the data year.
Apply the $50,000 participation threshold and the NAIC participating-state list to derive your own in-scope population.
Do this before looking at the preparer's scoping worksheet.
Record your population with the premium figure behind each state/line.
testing.done: an auditor-derived in-scope population exists, built from filed statements without reference to the preparer's scoping.

testing.step: Reconcile the auditor population to what was actually filed
actions: In iSite+ open the MCAS application submission history and list every state/line actually submitted for the data year.
Compare against your derived population: any in-scope state/line with no submission is a missed-filing exception; any out-of-scope submission is noted.
Compare your population to the preparer's scoping worksheet and list scoping differences separately.
Document both reconciliations in the workpaper.
testing.done: submission history reconciles to the independent population with missed filings and scoping differences listed.

testing.step: Verify timeliness against the April 30 deadline
actions: Read the submission timestamp on each iSite+ confirmation, not the tracking sheet.
Compare every timestamp to April 30 of the filing year; list any late submission with its day count.
Check any resubmission's date and whether the state requested it or the company self-corrected.
Capture confirmation screenshots into the workpaper.
testing.done: every filing's timeliness is verified from the confirmation itself with late filings and resubmissions listed.

testing.step: Draw the data-element sample
actions: Select 5 state/line filings: the 2 largest by premium, 1 with a flagged ratio movement, and 2 at random with a recorded seed.
Within each, select 6 data elements spanning claims counts, timeliness medians, lawsuits and cancellations/nonrenewals.
Record seed, selection date and the element list for re-drawability.
Pull the retained extracts and mapping book for the sampled filings.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of 5 filings and 30 data elements is drawn with source extracts pulled.

testing.step: Re-derive sampled data elements from source systems
actions: For each sampled element, write an independent query against the enterprise data warehouse (or direct source system) applying the NAIC Data Call & Definitions text yourself.
Compare your derived value to the submitted value; a difference over 1% is an exception.
Where your value differs, determine whether the mapping book or the extract job caused it.
Save queries and outputs in the workpaper.
testing.done: all 30 sampled elements are independently re-derived with differences over 1% logged and attributed.

testing.step: Trace claim-level detail behind the counts
actions: For 10 claims inside sampled counts, open the claim files in the Claims Platform and verify state, line, open/close dates and payment amounts match the MCAS categorization.
Specifically verify claims counted as closed without payment meet the MCAS definition rather than the internal closure code.
Verify median-days elements by recomputing the day counts for the traced claims.
List any miscategorized claim as an exception.
testing.done: ten claims trace from submitted counts to source files with categorization and day counts verified.

testing.step: Verify validation, interrogatories and attestation evidence
actions: For sampled filings, inspect the retained validation output and confirm all errors were cleared before attestation.
Read the interrogatory answers against the mapping book for internal consistency.
Confirm the attestation was completed by the registered Attestor and dates after the validation package sign-off.
Note any attestation preceding validation as a control exception.
testing.done: validation clearance, consistent interrogatories and a properly sequenced attestation are evidenced for each sampled filing.

testing.step: Check the Bermuda SFR coordination held
actions: Obtain the BMA filing confirmation for the statutory financial return and compare the filing date to the 4-months-after-year-end deadline under s.17–s.18.
Verify the recorded calendar-alignment agreement existed before both data cuts.
Confirm neither filing was delayed by the shared resource plan; where one slipped, read the escalation trail.
Record findings in the workpaper.
testing.done: both the MCAS and SFR filings verify as on time with the coordination agreement evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception: missed states, late filings, element misstatements over 1%, miscategorized claims, sequencing failures.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date; misstatements route to the mapping-book owner.
For misstatements material to a state's ratios, have Regulatory Counsel assess whether a corrected resubmission should be volunteered.
Carry open issues into next cycle's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception is tracked with owner and date, and material misstatements carry a counsel resubmission assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute results against the thresholds (100% on-time filings, ≤1% element variance) and write the conclusion with workpaper references.
Have the Chief Audit Executive, who prepared no tested filing, review and sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and exceptions to the Compliance Committee.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C27.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Refresh the metric definitions and benchmark sources for the quarter
actions: Open the Conduct Metrics Monitoring Procedure and confirm each metric's formula and threshold are unchanged; where the NAIC has published new industry medians or complaint-index results, update the benchmark column.
Download and date-stamp the benchmark sources: NAIC complaint index for each writing company from the NAIC CIS pages, published MCAS industry results, and any new BMA conduct guidance from bma.bm.
Record the benchmark version used this quarter in the pack's source appendix.
Route any threshold change to the Head of Compliance for approval before use.
checklist.done: the quarter's formulas, thresholds and dated benchmark captures are fixed and any threshold change is approved.

checklist.step: Verify the data feeds behind the dashboard are complete for the quarter
actions: Check the warehouse load logs for the claims, complaints and policy feeds covering the full quarter, confirming the last load date is on or after quarter end.
Reconcile quarterly claim counts in the warehouse to a direct Claims Platform query and complaint counts to the workflow/case management tool register, tolerance zero.
Investigate and clear any feed gap before metrics are computed; a stale feed quarter must be flagged on the pack cover.
Log the reconciliation in the pack workpapers.
checklist.done: all three feeds are complete through quarter end and reconcile to source at zero tolerance.

checklist.step: Compute complaint metrics and the complaint-index position
actions: From the complaints register pull the quarter's complaints by product, state/jurisdiction, root-cause code and channel, splitting regulator-forwarded complaints from direct ones.
Compute complaints per 1,000 policies in force and the trend against the prior four quarters.
Record the latest NAIC complaint index for each writing company and note whether the company sits above 1.0 (worse than average share) in any line.
Verify acknowledgement and resolution timeliness percentages against the timeframes in the complaints procedure.
checklist.done: complaint volumes, ratios, index positions and timeliness percentages are computed with four-quarter trends.

checklist.step: Compute claims-conduct metrics
actions: From the Claims Platform data pull the quarter's median days report-to-acknowledgement, report-to-decision and decision-to-payment by line.
Compute the denial rate and the claims-closed-without-payment percentage per line using the MCAS definitions so quarters reconcile to the annual MCAS filing.
Compute litigation rate (suits opened per 1,000 claims closed) and interim-payment usage on long-tail claims.
Compare each metric to its threshold and to the MCAS industry median where one exists.
checklist.done: claims cycle, denial, closure and litigation metrics are computed on MCAS-consistent definitions and compared to thresholds.

checklist.step: Compute policyholder-treatment and producer-conduct metrics
actions: From policy administration data compute cancellation and nonrenewal rates by state and line, separating company-initiated from customer-initiated.
Pull producer conduct flags from the quarter: complaint-linked producers, unauthorized-business exceptions from the REG-057-C25 reconciliation, and terminated-for-cause counts.
Compute free-look cancellation rates and replacement activity for life/annuity lines as mis-selling indicators.
Compare each metric to threshold and prior quarters.
checklist.done: treatment and producer metrics are computed with company/customer splits and mis-selling indicators included.

checklist.step: Rate every metric against amber and red thresholds
actions: In the Power BI conduct dashboard apply the quarter's data cut and read the RAG status the threshold rules assign to each metric.
Manually verify the RAG assignment for every metric within 5% of its threshold — boundary cases must not ride on a rounding rule.
Write a one-paragraph narrative per amber/red metric naming the driver (volume, mix, process, data).
Freeze the dashboard view as the quarter's pack exhibit.
checklist.done: every metric carries a verified RAG status and every amber/red carries a driver narrative in the frozen exhibit.

checklist.step: Escalate red-threshold breaches within 5 business days
actions: For each red metric, send a written escalation to the Head of Compliance and the accountable business owner within 5 business days of the dashboard cut.
State in the escalation: the metric, threshold, actual value, affected jurisdictions and the proposed investigation owner.
Open an investigation task per breach in the tracker with a 20-business-day due date.
Record the escalation dates on the pack cover.
checklist.done: every red breach shows a dated escalation inside 5 business days and an owned investigation task.

checklist.step: Investigate each red breach to root cause
actions: Drill the breached metric to case level — e.g. list the individual claims driving a cycle-time breach with adjuster, line and state.
Interview the responsible manager and classify the root cause: staffing, process change, system defect, data error or genuine conduct issue.
Where the cause is a data error, correct the source and recompute the metric; where genuine, agree corrective actions with dates.
Write the investigation memo and attach the case-level evidence.
checklist.done: each breach has an investigation memo with case-level drill-down, a classified root cause and dated corrective actions.

checklist.step: Check whether any breach triggers regulator-facing obligations
actions: Review each red-breach memo against the BMA Insurance Code of Conduct and state requirements for whether the finding amounts to a matter requiring notification or self-report.
Assess whether any state's claims-handling or unfair-trade-practices rules require remediation of affected policyholders (e.g. re-adjudication or interest on late payments).
Document the notify/do-not-notify decision with reasons, and where notification is due, agree the channel and timing with the Head of Compliance and the Principal Representative for BMA matters.
File the counsel memo with the investigation record.
checklist.done: every red breach carries a documented counsel decision on notification and policyholder remediation.

checklist.step: Compile the quarterly conduct-metrics pack
actions: Assemble the pack: RAG summary page, per-metric trend charts, benchmark appendix with dated source captures, breach escalations and investigation statuses.
Include the reconciliation sign-off from the data feed check as the pack's data-quality statement.
Have the Head of Compliance review and sign the pack within 25 business days of quarter end.
Distribute to the Chief Claims Officer, Head of Distribution and Complaints Manager for their metric areas.
checklist.done: a signed pack with trends, benchmarks and breach status is distributed inside the 25-business-day window.

checklist.step: Present the pack at the conduct governance forum
actions: Table the quarterly pack at the conduct governance forum and upload the summary to the board portal for the Risk/Compliance Committee.
Walk the forum through every red metric, its investigation and corrective actions, and any counsel notification decision.
Minute challenges and directed actions with named owners.
Add directed actions to the tracker referencing the forum date.
checklist.done: the forum has minuted the pack review with directed actions tracked to owners.

checklist.step: Track corrective actions from prior quarters to closure
actions: Pull all open conduct-metric corrective actions from the tracker and chase each owner for status ahead of the pack cut.
Verify claimed closures against evidence — a metric returning inside threshold for two consecutive quarters is the closure standard for process fixes.
Report overdue actions by owner and age in the quarterly pack.
Escalate actions overdue more than one quarter to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: all corrective actions show verified status, closures meet the two-quarter standard, and overdue items are escalated.

checklist.step: Feed conduct-metric intelligence into exam readiness and procedures
actions: Hand persistent outlier metrics and their investigation memos to the exam-readiness file maintained under REG-057-C29.
Where an investigation exposed a procedure defect, raise the procedure amendment into the REG-057-C26 review cycle by document id.
Where MCAS-visible ratios moved materially, alert the Regulatory Reporting Manager so next year's MCAS validation expects the movement.
Record the cross-references in the pack appendix.
checklist.done: outliers, procedure defects and MCAS-visible movements are cross-fed to C29, C26 and C27 with references recorded.

checklist.step: Review threshold calibration annually
actions: Once a year, compare each metric's threshold to the newest NAIC industry medians, complaint-index distributions and BMA expectations.
Tighten thresholds where the company has sat comfortably green for four quarters and the benchmark has moved; document the rationale for each change.
Approve the recalibrated threshold set into the Conduct Metrics Monitoring Procedure.
Note the calibration date in the procedure header.
checklist.done: thresholds are recalibrated against current benchmarks with documented rationale and an approved procedure update.

checklist.step: Archive the quarter's monitoring evidence
actions: Upload the signed pack, frozen dashboard exhibit, feed reconciliations, escalations, investigation memos and counsel decisions to the compliance evidence repository.
Index under REG-057-C28 / <yyyy>Q<n> with the 7-year retention label.
Run a retrieval check by pulling one prior quarter's breach investigation from the index.
Close the compliance calendar task with the repository link.
checklist.done: the quarter's full evidence set is filed with 7-year retention and passes a retrieval check.

testing.step: Build the population of packs, metrics and breaches for the year
actions: Pull all four quarterly packs for the year from the compliance evidence repository index under REG-057-C28.
List every metric per pack with its value, threshold, RAG status and any escalation reference.
List every red breach and its investigation and counsel-decision records.
Record counts and any missing pack or missing investigation as an immediate exception.
testing.done: a complete inventory of packs, metric values and breach records exists with gaps flagged.

testing.step: Reconcile pack production timing to the procedure standard
actions: For each quarter, compare the Head of Compliance signature date to quarter end and test the 25-business-day standard.
Compare each red-breach escalation date to the dashboard cut date and test the 5-business-day standard.
Verify dates from document metadata and email timestamps, not from the pack cover statements.
List every blown window with its actual day count.
testing.done: pack and escalation timeliness is verified from metadata with blown windows counted.

testing.step: Draw the metric sample for recomputation
actions: Select 12 metric values across the four packs: every red metric, at least two ambers, and greens drawn at random with a recorded seed.
Ensure the sample covers complaints, claims cycle, denial rate and cancellation/nonrenewal families.
Record seed, population and selection date for re-drawability.
Pull the frozen dashboard exhibits and feed reconciliations for the sampled quarters.
testing.done: a reproducible 12-value sample spanning all metric families and every red is drawn.

testing.step: Recompute sampled metrics from source systems
actions: For each sampled value, write an independent query against the warehouse (or the Claims Platform / complaints register directly) applying the procedure's formula yourself.
Compare your value to the pack value; any difference beyond rounding is an exception.
Where a difference appears, decide whether the dashboard rule, the feed or the manual pack transcription caused it.
Save queries and outputs in the workpaper.
testing.done: all sampled metrics recompute from source with differences attributed to dashboard, feed or transcription.

testing.step: Verify benchmark values against their published sources
actions: For each sampled metric with a benchmark, open the cited source — the NAIC complaint index page, published MCAS industry results or BMA guidance — as of the pack's stated capture date.
Compare the benchmark figure in the pack to the published figure; a stale or transcribed-wrong benchmark is an exception.
Confirm the benchmark version in the source appendix matches what was actually used in the RAG rule.
Capture the source pages into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled benchmark traces to its published source at the stated version.

testing.step: Re-perform the RAG assignment on boundary cases
actions: Identify every sampled metric within 5% of its threshold and re-apply the threshold rule to the recomputed value.
Confirm no red was downgraded to amber by rounding, threshold misstatement or a mid-year unapproved threshold change.
Check the threshold used matches the version approved by the Head of Compliance for that quarter.
List any wrong RAG as an exception — a suppressed red is a reportable finding.
testing.done: boundary RAG assignments are re-performed against approved thresholds with any suppressed red reported.

testing.step: Test breach investigations to case-level evidence
actions: For each red breach, open the investigation memo and trace its case-level drill-down: re-open 3 of the cited cases in the Claims Platform or complaints register and confirm they support the stated root cause.
Verify corrective actions have named owners, dates and closure evidence meeting the two-consecutive-green-quarters standard.
Confirm the counsel notification decision exists and pre-dates pack sign-off.
List investigations resting on unverifiable cases as exceptions.
testing.done: every red-breach investigation traces to real cases, dated corrective actions and a timely counsel decision.

testing.step: Verify governance visibility of the packs
actions: Pull the conduct governance forum minutes for each quarter and confirm the pack was tabled and reds were discussed.
Confirm the summary reached the Risk/Compliance Committee via the board portal for each quarter.
Trace two directed actions from minutes into the tracker and to their current status.
Note any quarter where reds were not minuted as an exception.
testing.done: all four packs trace to forum minutes and committee papers with directed actions tracked.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception, splitting computation errors, stale benchmarks, timeliness misses, RAG suppression and unverifiable investigations.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date.
Route any suppressed red or missed notification decision to Regulatory Counsel for a disclosure assessment.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception is tracked with owner and date, and suppression or notification misses carry a counsel assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute results against the thresholds (four timely packs, 100% escalated reds, exact recomputation) and write the conclusion with workpaper references.
Have the Chief Audit Executive, who produced no tested pack, review and sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Compliance Committee alongside the Q4 pack.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C28.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the committee.
