checklist.step: Maintain the exam-file index mapped to examiner standards
actions: Structure the repository exam library by the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook standard areas (operations/management, complaint handling, marketing and sales, producer licensing, policyholder service, underwriting and rating, claims) plus a BMA inspection section for governance and Code of Conduct evidence.
For each index row record: artifact name, repository link, owner role, last refresh date, maximum staleness interval.
Review the index monthly and chase owners whose artifacts approach 80% of their staleness interval.
Version the index so its state at any past date can be reproduced.
checklist.done: a versioned index maps every Handbook and BMA scope area to a current artifact with owner and staleness dates.

checklist.step: Keep procedure and governance artifacts current in the file
actions: Link the exam file to the live conduct procedure library maintained under REG-057-C26 rather than copying documents, so examiners always receive the approved current version.
File the current organizational charts, conduct governance terms of reference and committee minutes covering conduct topics for the trailing 24 months.
File the current s.8A Declaration of Compliance and the completion certificate behind it.
Refresh governance artifacts quarterly and stamp the refresh date on the index.
checklist.done: procedure links resolve to current approved versions and governance artifacts are stamped within the quarter.

checklist.step: Keep licensing, appointment and producer records exam-ready
actions: File each quarter's producer reconciliation report from REG-057-C25 with its exception log and remediation status.
Keep a current extract of appointed producers by state and the BMA intermediary register captures.
Ensure terminated-for-cause files include the state notification evidence examiners routinely request.
Stamp the refresh date on the index each quarter.
checklist.done: licensing artifacts are quarterly-stamped, with for-cause files carrying their state notifications.

checklist.step: Keep complaint and claims evidence continuously loaded
actions: Export the complaints register quarterly (complaint id, dates, jurisdiction, root cause, resolution, timeliness) into the exam file in the format examiners request in data calls.
File the quarterly conduct-metrics packs from REG-057-C28 including breach investigations.
File claims letter templates (denial, reservation of rights, delay) as currently in force in the Claims Platform, with their version dates.
Verify the complaint export row count matches the register before filing.
checklist.done: complaint exports, metrics packs and current letter templates are filed quarterly with counts verified.

checklist.step: Maintain the prior-exam and inspection history section
actions: File every prior state market conduct exam report, BMA inspection letter and the company's responses.
Maintain a findings register: each prior finding, the committed remediation, evidence of completion and current status — examiners test repeat findings first.
Cross-check the findings register against REG-057-C30's remediation log so statuses never diverge.
Review the section semi-annually and stamp the index.
checklist.done: the exam history section holds all prior reports with a findings register reconciled to the C30 remediation log.

checklist.step: Maintain the examiner logistics playbook and interview roster
actions: Keep the first-48-hours protocol current: who receives an exam call or s.29 notice, who notifies the Head of Compliance, Regulatory Counsel and (for BMA) the Principal Representative, and who stands up the request log.
Maintain the interview roster: for each Handbook area, the manager who can speak to it, with a trained deputy.
Keep on-site logistics ready: examiner workspace, system read-only access request templates for the Claims Platform and policy administration system.
Walk a new joiner through the protocol whenever the roster changes.
checklist.done: the protocol, interview roster and logistics templates are current with every named person still in role.

checklist.step: Stand up the request log on any exam or notice
actions: On receipt of an exam call letter, data call or s.29 notice, open a request log in the tracker: one row per requested item with the examiner's reference, due date, assigned owner and status.
Circulate a document hold notice to affected teams the same day so nothing responsive is altered or deleted.
Set daily stand-ups with item owners while requests are open.
Record receipt date and due date of the notice itself as row zero.
checklist.done: every incoming request lives as a logged row with owner, due date and a same-day hold notice issued.

checklist.step: Route every production through privilege and accuracy review
actions: Review each outgoing document set for privileged material and for consistency with prior productions before release.
Confirm data extracts were run by the named owner from the system of record and reconcile to the counts stated in the cover response.
Log the reviewed-and-released decision per item on the request log with the release date.
Keep an exact copy of everything produced, as produced, in the exam file.
checklist.done: no item leaves without a logged counsel review, and produced sets are archived exactly as released.

checklist.step: Answer examiner requests inside their stated deadlines
actions: Track each request-log row against its due date daily and escalate any row at risk to the Head of Compliance 3 business days before it falls due.
Where a deadline genuinely cannot be met, have counsel request an extension in writing before the due date — never after.
Record actual delivery dates against due dates on the log.
Close each row only when the examiner acknowledges receipt.
checklist.done: every request row shows delivery on or before its due date, or a pre-deadline written extension.

checklist.step: Run the annual unannounced readiness drill
actions: Once a year, issue a mock data call built from a real state exam call letter (complaint register extract, producer list, denial-letter sample, procedure set) without advance warning to the file owners.
Time the response: the standard is a complete, accurate production within 5 business days.
Score the drill on completeness, accuracy and timeliness, and record misses per artifact.
Feed each miss into the exception log with an owner and fix date.
checklist.done: a timed unannounced drill is scored with every miss logged and owned.

checklist.step: Refresh staleness measurements and chase owners quarterly
actions: Run the repository staleness report: every artifact's last refresh date against its interval.
Chase each overdue owner in writing with a 10-business-day cure window.
Compute the file health percentage (artifacts in-date / total) for the quarterly health report.
Log artifacts still stale after the cure window as exceptions.
checklist.done: quarterly staleness is measured, owners chased, and post-cure stale artifacts are logged exceptions.

checklist.step: Brief interview-roster managers on current exam themes
actions: Twice a year, brief every interview-roster manager on their area's current metrics, open findings and likely examiner questions drawn from recent NAIC exam trends and BMA inspection themes.
Rehearse the rule: answer what is asked, factually, and route document commitments through the exam coordinator.
Record attendance and update the roster where a manager or deputy has changed.
File the briefing materials in the exam file.
checklist.done: all roster managers are briefed within the half-year with attendance recorded and materials filed.

checklist.step: Log readiness exceptions with disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every stale artifact past cure, drill miss and late request response, with root cause and owner.
Distinguish process causes (refresh cadence too loose) from ownership causes (role vacancy) — the fixes differ.
Set remediation dates and review open items monthly.
Close only on evidence: the refreshed artifact, the passed retest or the delivered response.
checklist.done: every readiness exception is tracked with root cause, owner and evidence-based closure.

checklist.step: Issue the quarterly exam-file health report
actions: Compile the health report: file health percentage, open exceptions, drill results, active exams and request-log performance.
Sign it and table it at the conduct governance forum with the REG-057-C28 metrics pack.
Minute directed actions and track them to owners.
File the signed report in the exam file.
checklist.done: a signed quarterly health report is tabled, minuted and filed.

checklist.step: Capture lessons learned after every exam or inspection
actions: Within 30 days of an exam report or BMA inspection letter, hold a lessons-learned review: which requests strained the file, which artifacts were stale, which interviews went poorly.
Amend the Exam Readiness Procedure, index structure and refresh intervals accordingly.
Hand every finding to REG-057-C30 for remediation tracking by finding reference.
File the lessons-learned memo in the exam history section.
checklist.done: a lessons-learned memo exists within 30 days of each exam with procedure amendments made and findings handed to C30.

testing.step: Pull the exam-file index and build the artifact population
actions: Export the current exam-file index from the compliance evidence repository with every artifact's owner, last refresh date and staleness interval.
Independently list the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook standard areas and BMA inspection scope areas and check each is represented in the index.
Record the artifact count and any unrepresented scope area as an immediate coverage exception.
Save the export as the tested population.
testing.done: the index export is the tested population with unrepresented examiner scope areas flagged.

testing.step: Reconcile the index to the repository contents
actions: Open every 5th index row's repository link and confirm the artifact exists, is the version the index claims, and is readable.
List broken links, wrong versions and access failures as exceptions.
Confirm procedure links resolve to the live approved versions in the document management repository, not stale copies.
Document the link-check results in the workpaper.
testing.done: sampled index links resolve to the claimed current artifacts with failures listed.

testing.step: Measure staleness independently at the test date
actions: Recompute each artifact's staleness from repository metadata dates, not the index's recorded refresh dates.
Compute the file health percentage and compare to the ≥95% threshold and to the quarterly health reports' claimed figures.
Where the health report claimed a higher figure than metadata supports, treat the difference as a reporting exception.
Record the measurement in the workpaper.
testing.done: file health is independently measured from metadata and reconciled to the reported figures.

testing.step: Run an independent retrieval drill
actions: Compose a 10-item request set from a real exam call letter format — complaint register extract for a named quarter, appointed-producer list for two states, three denial letters, the claims-conduct procedure in force on a named past date.
Issue it to the exam coordinator without notice and time the response against the 5-business-day standard.
Verify the returned items for accuracy: complaint counts against the register, the past-dated procedure against version history.
Score completeness, accuracy and timeliness per item.
testing.done: an auditor-issued drill is scored per item with timing measured against the 5-day standard.

testing.step: Test the year's real examiner and BMA requests for timeliness
actions: Pull every request-log row from the year's exams, data calls and s.29 notices.
Compare each delivery date to the stated due date, verifying delivery from sent-mail or portal timestamps rather than the log field.
Confirm any late row carries a pre-deadline written extension from counsel.
List late-without-extension rows as exceptions.
testing.done: every real request row's timeliness is verified from timestamps with unexcused lateness listed.

testing.step: Verify privilege review and production archiving
actions: For 5 sampled produced items, confirm the request log shows a counsel reviewed-and-released decision dated before the delivery date.
Open the archived as-produced copy and confirm it matches the delivery (same file hash or identical content).
Confirm the document hold notice for each exam was issued the day the notice arrived.
List missing reviews, missing archives or late holds as exceptions.
testing.done: sampled productions show pre-dated counsel review, exact archives and same-day hold notices.

testing.step: Verify the prior-findings register against source reports
actions: Take the two most recent exam/inspection reports and list every finding directly from the report text.
Match each to a findings-register row and to a REG-057-C30 remediation record; a finding absent from either is an exception.
Check register statuses against closure evidence rather than status labels.
Document the trace in the workpaper.
testing.done: every finding in the two latest reports traces to a register row and a C30 remediation record with evidenced status.

testing.step: Verify drill history and briefing cadence
actions: Confirm the annual unannounced drill ran, was scored and its misses entered the exception log with owners.
Confirm two interview-roster briefings ran in the year with attendance records covering every roster manager.
Check roster names against current HR records for leavers not replaced.
List missed drills, briefings or roster gaps as exceptions.
testing.done: drill and briefing cadences are evidenced and the roster contains no unreplaced leavers.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception: coverage gaps, broken links, staleness, drill failures, unexcused late responses, register mismatches.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date.
Route any late response to a live regulator request to Regulatory Counsel for relationship-impact assessment.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception is tracked with owner and date, and live-request lateness carries a counsel assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute results against the thresholds (≥95% health, 100% timely responses, 5-day drill) and write the conclusion with workpaper references.
Have the Chief Audit Executive, who maintains no exam-file artifact, review and sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Compliance Committee with the drill scorecard.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C29.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and drill scorecard is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Intake every finding within 5 business days of the report
actions: On receipt of an exam report or BMA inspection letter, extract every numbered finding, recommendation and required action verbatim into one tracker issue each.
Record on each issue: source report reference, finding text, cited law or Code paragraph, regulator's required deadline, and severity as the regulator graded it.
Record the report's overall response deadline (state reports commonly 30 days; BMA letters commonly 14 days) as its own master issue.
Cross-reference each issue to the exam-readiness findings register maintained under REG-057-C29.
checklist.done: every finding is a tracker issue with verbatim text, citation, deadline and severity, logged within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Convene the response team and assign finding owners
actions: Within 10 business days, convene Regulatory Counsel, the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and each affected business head to walk every finding.
Assign each finding a single accountable business owner at manager level or above — never 'Compliance' as the owner of a business-process fix.
Decide per finding: accept, seek clarification, or contest with evidence; counsel drafts any contest.
Minute the meeting with owners and decisions per finding.
checklist.done: every finding has a named accountable owner and an accept/clarify/contest decision minuted.

checklist.step: Draft the formal response within the regulator's deadline
actions: Draft the response letter addressing every finding: the corrective commitment, the target date and the responsible executive.
Verify each committed date against the owner's written confirmation that it is achievable — never commit a date the owner has not accepted.
Route for signature: Head of Compliance for state reports, the Principal Representative for BMA letters, then submit through the regulator's stated channel before the deadline.
File the submitted response and delivery proof on the master issue.
checklist.done: a signed response committing owner-confirmed dates for every finding is submitted before the regulator's deadline with proof filed.

checklist.step: Build a milestone action plan per finding
actions: With each owner, decompose the committed fix into milestones with dates: root-cause analysis, design of the fix, implementation, and an evidence-of-operation period.
Define per finding the closure evidence standard up front — e.g. for a claims-timeliness finding: revised procedure, retrained staff list, and 90 days of cycle-time data inside standard.
Load milestones onto the tracker issue so the T-30/T-14/T-3 alerts arm automatically.
Have the Head of Compliance approve each plan against the committed regulator date, with buffer.
checklist.done: every finding carries an approved milestone plan with a pre-agreed closure evidence standard and armed alerts.

checklist.step: Run root-cause analysis before designing the fix
actions: For each finding, analyze whether the cause is procedure content, training, staffing, system configuration or oversight failure, using case-level data from the affected system (Claims Platform, complaints register, policy administration).
Test the breadth: query whether the same failure exists in states or lines the exam did not sample — regulators expect the fix to cover the full footprint, not the sampled slice.
Document the root cause and breadth conclusion on the tracker issue.
Where breadth analysis finds unexamined instances, flag to Regulatory Counsel for a self-report decision.
checklist.done: each finding has a documented root cause and a breadth conclusion, with unexamined instances routed to counsel.

checklist.step: Execute remediation and capture evidence as milestones complete
actions: Chase each owner at every milestone date and collect the milestone's evidence immediately — procedure versions, system change tickets, training completion reports, corrected letter templates.
File evidence on the tracker issue and in the compliance evidence repository per-finding pack as it arrives, never retrospectively.
Mark milestones complete only with evidence attached; a verbal 'done' does not move status.
Update the finding's forecast date whenever a milestone slips.
checklist.done: milestones move to complete only with contemporaneous evidence attached and forecasts stay current.

checklist.step: Remediate affected policyholders where findings require it
actions: Where a finding involves customer harm (underpaid claims, wrongful denials, missed interest), build the affected-policyholder population from the source system with the query documented.
Compute the redress per policyholder — including statutory interest where a state's claims-payment law sets a rate — and have the Controller approve the payment run.
Issue payments and corrective letters, tracking returned mail and uncashed payments to resolution.
Report redress totals and completion status on the tracker issue.
checklist.done: the affected population is documented, redress computed with interest, payments issued and completion reported.

checklist.step: Hold the weekly at-risk review while findings are open
actions: Review every Monday the consolidated at-risk report: findings with milestones due in 30 days, slipped milestones and forecast breaches of regulator dates.
For any forecast breach of a committed regulator date, direct either recovery actions or a counsel-drafted extension request — submitted before the date, never after.
Record decisions on the affected tracker issues.
Escalate persistent slippage to the accountable executive's superior.
checklist.done: the weekly review runs with decisions recorded and no regulator date passes without recovery or a pre-dated extension request.

checklist.step: Submit regulator progress reports on the agreed schedule
actions: Where the regulator set a progress-report cadence, draft each report from tracker status: per finding, milestones completed, evidence available and forecast closure date.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear and the designated signatory sign each report; submit through the stated channel by the scheduled date.
State nothing as complete that lacks filed evidence — progress reports are testable statements.
File each submitted report and delivery proof on the master issue.
checklist.done: every scheduled progress report is submitted on time, evidence-backed and filed with delivery proof.

checklist.step: Verify each finding independently before declaring closure
actions: When an owner declares a finding remediated, test it against the pre-agreed closure evidence standard: re-perform the fixed process on live cases or re-run the metric over the evidence-of-operation period.
Confirm the fix covers the full breadth identified in root-cause analysis, not just the examined states.
Issue a written verification memo — pass or fail — on the tracker issue.
Failed verifications reset the finding to open with the gap documented.
checklist.done: every closure carries an independent verification memo confirming the evidence standard and breadth are met.

checklist.step: Obtain closure sign-off and notify the regulator
actions: Sign each verified finding closed, referencing the verification memo.
Where the regulator requires closure notification, have counsel draft it citing the evidence held, signed by the designated signatory.
Update the REG-057-C29 findings register to closed with the verification reference so exam files stay consistent.
Retain the regulator's acknowledgement when received.
checklist.done: closed findings show sign-off, a consistent C29 register entry and, where required, an acknowledged regulator notification.

checklist.step: Log deviations on the finding record
actions: Log every missed milestone, extension request, failed verification and reopened finding as a deviation entry on the finding's issue with root cause.
Track deviation counts by owner and report them in the monthly compliance dashboard.
Treat a second miss on the same finding as an automatic escalation to the accountable executive.
Keep the deviation history permanently with the finding pack.
checklist.done: every deviation is logged with root cause, trends are reported by owner, and repeat misses auto-escalate.

checklist.step: Monitor sustainability after closure
actions: For each closed finding with a measurable metric, monitor that metric for two further quarters through the REG-057-C28 conduct-metrics pack.
Reopen the finding if the metric regresses through its threshold within the monitoring window.
Record the end-of-monitoring confirmation on the tracker issue.
Summarize sustainability outcomes in the annual remediation review.
checklist.done: closed findings show two quarters of sustained metrics or a documented reopening.

checklist.step: Report remediation status to governance
actions: Report monthly to the Risk/Compliance Committee via the board portal: open findings by severity and age, regulator dates at risk, closures this period and redress totals.
Flag any finding whose regulator date is at risk in the next 60 days for committee attention.
Minute directed actions with owners.
File the committee papers with the remediation records.
checklist.done: monthly committee reporting shows the full open book with at-risk dates flagged and directed actions minuted.

checklist.step: Archive per-finding packs and run the annual lessons review
actions: Maintain each finding's pack in the compliance evidence repository: report extract, response, action plan, milestone evidence, verification memo, closure sign-off and correspondence, indexed under REG-057-C30 / finding reference.
Apply permanent retention while citable, minimum 7 years.
Annually, review closed findings for recurring root causes and feed systemic themes into the REG-057-C26 procedure cycle.
Confirm a retrieval check pulls one full pack by finding reference.
checklist.done: complete per-finding packs are archived with retention applied and the annual root-cause review is fed to C26.

testing.step: Build the finding population from source reports, not the tracker
actions: Collect every exam report and BMA inspection letter received in the trailing 24 months from the exam history section of the C29 file and from Regulatory Counsel's correspondence records.
List every numbered finding directly from the report texts.
Record report receipt dates from delivery evidence (email/courier timestamps).
This list — not the tracker — is the tested population.
testing.done: an auditor-built finding list with receipt dates exists from source reports independently of the tracker.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the remediation log
actions: Match every source finding to a tracker issue; a finding with no issue is an intake-failure exception.
Compare each issue's creation date to the report receipt date against the 5-business-day intake standard.
Check the finding text on the issue is verbatim, not paraphrased in a way that narrows the obligation.
Document the reconciliation with exceptions listed.
testing.done: every source finding maps to a timely, verbatim tracker issue or is a listed exception.

testing.step: Verify response letters met the regulators' deadlines
actions: For each report, compare the response submission proof (portal receipt, email timestamp, courier record) to the deadline stated in the report or letter — 30 days for typical state reports, 14 days where BMA correspondence states it.
Confirm each response was signed by the correct signatory (Head of Compliance for states, Principal Representative for BMA).
Confirm every committed date in the response carried a pre-existing owner confirmation.
List late or wrongly signed responses as exceptions.
testing.done: every response verifies as on time, correctly signed and owner-confirmed from delivery evidence.

testing.step: Draw the finding sample for depth testing
actions: Select 100% of findings closed with a regulator during the year, plus a seeded random selection of open findings, minimum 12 findings total.
Include at least one finding with policyholder redress and one with a milestone slip if any exist.
Record seed, population and selection date for re-drawability.
Pull each sampled finding's full pack from the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all regulator-closed findings, a redress case and a slip case is drawn with packs pulled.

testing.step: Recompute milestone and deadline performance on the sample
actions: For each sampled finding, compare every milestone's completion evidence date to its planned date and recompute the on-time percentage against the ≥90% standard.
Verify completion dates from the evidence artifacts' own metadata, not the tracker status dates.
Confirm every slipped milestone has a deviation entry and every second slip an escalation record.
List undated or backdated evidence as exceptions.
testing.done: milestone performance is recomputed from artifact metadata with deviations and escalations verified.

testing.step: Re-verify closures reported to regulators
actions: For each finding reported closed to a regulator, re-perform the closure test against the pre-agreed evidence standard: re-run the metric over the evidence-of-operation window or re-inspect the fixed process on current cases.
Confirm the independent verification memo existed before the closure notification was sent.
Any closure notification sent without a pass verification memo is a reportable finding, not a mere exception.
Record re-verification results per finding.
testing.done: every regulator-reported closure re-verifies against its evidence standard with memo sequencing confirmed.

testing.step: Test policyholder redress completeness and accuracy
actions: For the sampled redress finding, re-run the affected-population query from its documentation and compare the count to the population actually paid.
Recompute redress for 5 policyholders including statutory interest at the state-specified rate and day count.
Trace the 5 payments to the payment system and confirm corrective letters went out.
List population shortfalls or computation differences as exceptions.
testing.done: the redress population reconciles and sampled payments recompute exactly with letters evidenced.

testing.step: Verify progress reports were accurate when sent
actions: For two submitted progress reports, take every 'complete' statement and confirm the supporting evidence existed in the repository on or before the report's submission date, using repository timestamps.
Confirm each report was cleared by counsel and signed by the designated signatory.
A 'complete' statement whose evidence post-dates the report is a misreporting exception routed to counsel.
Document the trace per statement.
testing.done: sampled progress-report statements trace to evidence pre-dating submission, with misreporting routed to counsel.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per test exception, distinguishing intake failures, deadline misses, unverified closures, redress shortfalls and misreporting.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date.
Route unverified closures and misreporting to Regulatory Counsel for a correction-to-regulator decision.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception is tracked with owner and date, and regulator-facing inaccuracies carry a counsel correction decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute results against the thresholds (100% timely intake, zero missed regulator deadlines, ≥90% milestones, zero unverified closures) and write the conclusion with workpaper references.
Have the Chief Audit Executive, who owned no tested finding, review and sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Risk/Compliance Committee with the monthly remediation status.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C30.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Download the current-year BSCR model and rule set from the BMA
actions: From bma.bm ▸ Regulatory Filings ▸ BSCR Models download the current-year BSCR Excel model for the entity's class (Class 4/3B) and the accompanying instructions.
Diff the new model's tabs and factor tables against last year's version and list every changed risk factor, new input field and revised correlation matrix.
Update the BSCR Production Procedure and data dictionary for each change, and brief the team on the deltas.
Record the model version and download date on the cycle cover sheet — populating an outdated version is a logged exception.
checklist.done: the current model version is confirmed, deltas from last year are documented and the procedure is updated.

checklist.step: Freeze the data cut and assemble source extracts
actions: Agree the data-cut date with the Controller aligned to the audited statutory year-end close.
Extract from the general ledger: investment holdings by asset class and rating, cash, receivables, and statutory balance sheet lines per the model's asset-classification instructions.
Request from the Reserving Actuary the net technical provisions by line and currency, and from the Catastrophe & Exposure Manager the net cat exposures and modeled losses.
Log every extract with run date, source system and row/total counts on the input register.
checklist.done: all source extracts are logged on the input register at an agreed cut aligned to the audited close.

checklist.step: Reconcile every model input to its source of record
actions: Tie total invested assets in the input pack to the general ledger investment balances at zero tolerance, with a bridge for market-value versus book-value fields as the instructions require.
Tie technical provisions to the Appointed Actuary's opinion figures and premium inputs to the statutory financial statements.
Have a second preparer initial each reconciliation; unresolved differences block model population.
File the reconciliation pack with the input register.
checklist.done: every input class ties to source at zero tolerance with dual initials and a filed reconciliation pack.

checklist.step: Populate the fixed-income and equity investment risk modules
actions: In the BSCR model's fixed-income tab, enter holdings by BSCR rating class using each security's rating mapped per the instructions' rating hierarchy.
Populate the equity tab by asset type (quoted, unquoted, real estate, affiliates) per the classification guidance.
Trace five securities from the custodian statement through the rating mapping to the entered class as a self-check.
Confirm the tab's computed charges change plausibly against last year given portfolio shifts, and note the movement commentary.
checklist.done: investment tabs are populated per the rating hierarchy with a five-security trace and movement commentary.

checklist.step: Populate the premium, reserve and catastrophe risk modules
actions: Enter net premium by BSCR line of business mapping the internal lines per the documented mapping table.
Enter net loss and loss-expense reserves by BSCR line from the reserving platform output.
Populate the catastrophe module with the net probable maximum loss figures from the licensed cat model output, applying the reinsurance program per the instructions.
Have the Reserving Actuary confirm the line mappings in writing for the cycle.
checklist.done: premium, reserve and cat modules are populated on confirmed line mappings with cat figures tied to model output.

checklist.step: Populate credit, concentration and operational risk inputs
actions: Enter reinsurance recoverables by counterparty rating band from the ceded reinsurance system, net of collateral per the collateral-recognition rules.
Populate the concentration tab with the ten largest asset exposures per the look-through requirements.
Complete the operational risk inputs from the corporate governance and risk-management questionnaire sections.
Cross-check counterparty ratings against the Reinsurance Credit & Security Analyst's current security list.
checklist.done: credit, concentration and operational inputs are populated with collateral netting and ratings cross-checked.

checklist.step: Run the model and derive the ECR
actions: Let the model aggregate the module charges through the BSCR correlation matrix and read the Basic BSCR and the ECR from the summary tab.
Verify the ECR equals the higher of the BSCR-derived requirement and the Minimum Solvency Margin per the Rules, and record both figures.
Compute the Target Capital Level as 120% of ECR.
Freeze and archive the populated model as bscr-<entity>-<yyyy>-final-draft.xlsx before review.
checklist.done: BSCR, ECR (with the MSM floor check), and TCL at 120% are derived and the model is frozen for review.

checklist.step: Tier eligible capital and test the limits
actions: Classify capital instruments into Tier 1/2/3 per the BMA Eligible Capital Rules, using each instrument's terms from the contract lifecycle repository.
Apply the tier limits against ECR and MSM (minimum Tier 1 proportions, Tier 3 caps) and compute eligible capital available.
Compute the coverage ratios: eligible capital / ECR and / TCL.
Have the Controller confirm the capital balances agree to the audited statutory statements.
checklist.done: capital is tiered per the Rules with limits tested and coverage ratios computed on Controller-confirmed balances.

checklist.step: Run the independent review gate before sign-off
actions: Have an actuary who populated no tab re-foot the module charges, re-trace ten inputs to source, and re-run the correlation aggregation on an independent copy.
Review the movement analysis: every module charge movement over 10% year-on-year must carry a written driver.
Confirm technical-provision inputs are consistent with the actuarial opinion being filed in the same return.
Document review points and their clearance on the review log.
checklist.done: an independent re-performance and movement review is documented with all points cleared.

checklist.step: Obtain executive sign-off on the capital result
actions: Present to the CFO and Chief Risk Officer: ECR, TCL, eligible capital, coverage ratios and the movement analysis.
Confirm coverage sits above the TCL; if coverage is below TCL or trending toward it, trigger the escalation path under REG-057-C32 before filing.
Obtain the CFO's written sign-off on the final figures.
Brief the board Audit/Risk Committee on the result ahead of filing.
checklist.done: the CFO has signed the final figures and the board committee is briefed, with any TCL shortfall escalated pre-filing.

checklist.step: Assemble and file the Capital and Solvency Return with the BMA
actions: Assemble the CSR package per the BMA checklist: the populated BSCR model, the CISSA (solvency self-assessment) schedules, the actuarial opinion and the required declarations.
Upload through the BMA's electronic filing portal against the entity's filing account, within 4 months of financial year end.
Download the portal acknowledgement and verify the submitted model file hash matches the signed-off version.
Record submission date, acknowledgement reference and the deadline margin on the cycle cover sheet.
checklist.done: the CSR is filed inside the 4-month deadline with an acknowledgement and a hash-verified model version.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly internal BSCR refresh
actions: Each quarter, refresh the model's material inputs (investments, reserves, premium, cat exposure) on unaudited balances within 20 business days of quarter end.
Recompute ECR, TCL and coverage, and deliver the results to the REG-057-C32 capital monitoring pack.
Flag any quarter where coverage moves more than 10 points or approaches TCL to the Head of Capital Management same day.
Archive each refresh with its input register.
checklist.done: quarterly refreshes deliver updated coverage to capital monitoring within 20 business days with movements flagged.

checklist.step: Manage any BMA queries or required restatement
actions: Answer BMA analytical queries on the filed BSCR from the archived model and reconciliation pack within the timeframe the query states.

If an error requiring restatement is found post-filing, quantify the ECR impact, have Regulatory Counsel clear the notification, and refile through the portal with the Principal Representative informed.
Log any restatement as an exception with root cause on the tracker.
File all query correspondence with the cycle evidence.
checklist.done: queries are answered from archived evidence on time and any restatement is cleared, refiled and logged.

checklist.step: Log cycle exceptions and update the procedure
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any late milestone, reconciliation break, review point cleared late, outdated-model use or restatement, with root cause and owner.
Hold a post-filing review within 30 days and write agreed improvements into the BSCR Production Procedure.
Route the updated procedure for Head of Capital Management and CRO approval.
Diary next cycle's model-version check for January.
checklist.done: cycle exceptions are tracked and the procedure is updated and re-approved within 30 days of filing.

checklist.step: Archive the complete capital calculation evidence pack
actions: Archive in the financial reporting repository: the filed model, input register and reconciliations, review log, sign-offs, CSR acknowledgement and quarterly refreshes.
Index under REG-057-C31 / <yyyy> with a 10-year retention label.
Run a retrieval check by pulling one module's input reconciliation from the index.
Close the capital calendar task with the repository link.
checklist.done: the full cycle pack is archived with 10-year retention and passes a retrieval check.

testing.step: Obtain the filed return and fix the tested versions
actions: Pull from the financial reporting repository the filed BSCR model, the CSR acknowledgement and the sign-off chain for the tested year.
Verify the archived model's file hash matches the filing acknowledgement reference so the tested artifact is the filed artifact.
Confirm the model version matches the BMA's published current-year version for the entity's class.
Record versions and hashes in the workpaper.
testing.done: the tested model is hash-verified as the filed version on the correct BMA model year.

testing.step: Verify filing timeliness against the statutory deadline
actions: Read the submission timestamp from the BMA portal acknowledgement.
Recompute the deadline as financial year end plus 4 months and compare.
Check whether any filing extension was requested and granted in writing before the deadline.
List any lateness with its day count.
testing.done: filing timeliness is verified from the acknowledgement against the recomputed 4-month deadline.

testing.step: Build the input population and reconcile to audited statements
actions: List every populated input tab of the filed model as the input population.
Independently tie total invested assets, technical provisions, premium and capital balances in the model to the audited statutory financial statements and general ledger.
Any input class that does not tie at zero tolerance is an exception regardless of size.
Document the tie-out with source references.
testing.done: model input classes independently tie to audited statements at zero tolerance or are listed exceptions.

testing.step: Draw the detailed input sample
actions: Select 25 line-level inputs across tabs with a recorded seed: 8 securities, 5 reserve lines, 4 premium lines, 4 reinsurance counterparties, 2 cat figures, 2 concentration exposures.
Weight the selection toward the largest charges and include every input the preparer flagged as judgmental.
Record seed, population and selection date for re-drawability.
Pull the source documents for each sampled input.
testing.done: a reproducible 25-input sample weighted to large and judgmental items is drawn with sources pulled.

testing.step: Re-perform classification on the sampled inputs
actions: For each sampled security, re-derive the BSCR rating class from the custodian statement and the instructions' rating hierarchy without reference to the preparer's mapping.
For sampled reserve and premium lines, re-apply the internal-to-BSCR line mapping from the reserving platform output.
For sampled counterparties, re-check the rating band and collateral netting against the security list and collateral agreements.
Every classification difference is an exception with its charge impact estimated.
testing.done: all 25 sampled inputs are independently reclassified with differences and charge impacts listed.

testing.step: Recompute module charges and the correlation aggregation
actions: On an independent copy of the official model, re-enter the verified inputs for two full modules (the largest market-risk module and one underwriting module) and compare computed charges to the filed model cell by cell.
Re-run the correlation matrix aggregation from the filed module charges and confirm the Basic BSCR reproduces exactly.
Check no factor table or formula in the filed model was altered from the BMA-published version by comparing formulas on the recomputed tabs.
Any non-reproducing figure or altered formula is a reportable exception.
testing.done: two modules and the aggregation reproduce exactly on an unaltered official model, or alterations are reported.

testing.step: Recompute ECR, MSM floor, TCL and coverage ratios
actions: Recompute the ECR as the higher of the BSCR result and the Minimum Solvency Margin, showing the MSM derivation per the Rules.
Recompute TCL = 120% × ECR and the coverage ratios from the tiered eligible capital schedule.
Re-perform the tier-limit tests on eligible capital against instrument terms from the contract repository.
Compare every recomputed figure to the filed and reported values exactly.
testing.done: ECR, MSM, TCL, tiering and coverage all recompute exactly to the filed figures.

testing.step: Verify review gates and sign-off sequencing
actions: Read the review log and confirm the independent actuarial review occurred and cleared its points before the CFO sign-off date.
Confirm the CFO sign-off pre-dates the portal submission timestamp.
Confirm the quarterly refreshes ran within 20 business days each quarter and fed the C32 monitoring pack.
List sequencing breaks and missed refreshes as exceptions.
testing.done: review, sign-off and filing dates sequence correctly and quarterly refreshes are evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception, splitting classification errors, non-reproducing computations, tie-out breaks and sequencing failures, each with estimated ECR impact.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date.
Where the aggregate impact could change the filed ECR materially, route to Regulatory Counsel and the Head of Capital Management for a restatement decision.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception is tracked with ECR impact, and material aggregates carry a restatement decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute results against the thresholds (on-time filing, zero-tolerance tie-outs, exact recomputation) and write the conclusion with workpaper references.
Have the Chief Audit Executive, who touched no model tab, review and sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit/Risk Committee alongside the capital adequacy report.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C31.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Maintain the trigger ladder above the regulatory intervention levels
actions: Set and annually re-approve the internal trigger ladder in the Capital Monitoring & Escalation Procedure: an amber trigger comfortably above the 120% TCL (e.g. board-approved appetite floor), a red trigger at TCL, and regulatory breach levels at ECR and MSM.
Reconcile the ladder to the current risk appetite statement approved by the board Risk Committee.
Record the ECR, TCL and MSM values from the latest filed BSCR (REG-057-C31) as the ladder's denominators.
Publish the approved ladder to the dashboard configuration and date-stamp it.
checklist.done: an approved trigger ladder tied to the latest filed ECR/TCL/MSM and the risk appetite statement is live in the dashboard.

checklist.step: Produce the monthly capital coverage estimate by working day 10
actions: Roll forward eligible capital from the latest quarter using the month's GL close: net income, investment valuation movements, dividends and any capital transactions from the Treasury Manager.
Adjust the ECR denominator for material risk-profile changes the estimation method names (large reinsurance program changes, major asset-mix shifts); otherwise hold the quarterly figure.
Compute estimated coverage = eligible capital / ECR and mark its position on the trigger ladder.
Publish the estimate to the dashboard and file the workbook by working day 10.
checklist.done: the monthly estimate is published to the dashboard by working day 10 with its roll-forward workbook filed.

checklist.step: Load the quarterly BSCR refresh as the anchor point
actions: Deliver the quarterly refreshed ECR, TCL and coverage from the REG-057-C31 refresh within 20 business days of quarter end.
Reconcile the quarter's monthly estimates against the refreshed figure and document the estimation error.
Where estimation error exceeds 5 coverage points, revise the estimation method and note the change in the procedure.
Reset the trigger ladder denominators to the refreshed ECR.
checklist.done: each quarter anchors the ladder to refreshed figures with estimation error measured and the method corrected if over 5 points.

checklist.step: Run daily awareness screening for capital-relevant events
actions: Maintain the event watchlist that can move capital between monthly estimates: catastrophe events touching the book, market shocks beyond defined thresholds, large loss advices, rating-agency actions on material reinsurers.
On any watchlist event, request a same-week ad-hoc coverage estimate from the Capital Management Manager.
Log each triggered ad-hoc estimate and its result in the GRC platform.
Brief the Chief Risk Officer on any ad-hoc estimate landing below amber.
checklist.done: watchlist events trigger logged ad-hoc estimates and sub-amber results reach the CRO.

checklist.step: Review the coverage dashboard at the monthly capital committee
actions: Chair the monthly capital committee reviewing the Power BI dashboard: current coverage, trend, distance to amber/red/ECR/MSM, and the drivers of movement.
Review forward-looking pressure: planned dividends, projected cat-season exposure and investment risk positioning against the trigger ladder.
Minute the committee's assessment and any pre-emptive actions (dividend deferral, retro purchase, de-risking).
File the minutes with the month's estimate.
checklist.done: the monthly committee minutes record coverage, forward pressure and any pre-emptive actions.

checklist.step: Escalate an amber trigger within the procedure's timetable
actions: On coverage crossing the amber trigger, open a breach event in the GRC platform the same day, recording the estimate, driver analysis and the ladder position.
Notify the CFO and CRO in writing within 2 business days with management options and their capital impact.
Increase estimation frequency to weekly until coverage recovers above amber for two consecutive estimates.
Record all steps with dates on the breach event.
checklist.done: amber events show same-day logging, 2-day CFO/CRO notification and weekly estimation until recovery.

checklist.step: Escalate a red (TCL) breach to the board
actions: On coverage falling below the 120% TCL, convene the board Risk Committee within 10 business days with a capital restoration options paper via the board portal.
Direct preparation of the capital plan: candidate actions (capital injection, reinsurance/retro, asset de-risking, dividend suspension) with amounts and timelines.
Anticipate BMA engagement: the Rules treat TCL as the supervisory early-warning level, so agree proactive communication with the Principal Representative and Regulatory Counsel.
Minute the board's chosen actions with owners and dates.
checklist.done: a TCL breach reaches the board inside 10 business days with a minuted restoration plan and a proactive BMA communication decision.

checklist.step: Notify the BMA within 14 days of any ECR failure
actions: On becoming aware that eligible capital has fallen below the ECR, start the GRC day-count timer immediately — the written notification to the BMA is due within 14 days of awareness.
Have Regulatory Counsel draft the notification stating the failure, its cause, the current coverage figures and the immediate management response; the Principal Representative and CFO sign.
Submit through the BMA's correspondence channel and retain delivery proof; record the awareness date, submission date and day count on the breach event.
Impose an immediate freeze on dividends and discretionary capital outflows pending the remediation plan.
checklist.done: the signed BMA notification is delivered within 14 days of awareness with the day count evidenced and outflows frozen.

checklist.step: File the remediation plan within 45 days of the ECR failure
actions: Build the remediation plan on the procedure's template: restoration actions, amounts, counterparties, milestones and the projected coverage path back above ECR and TCL.
Support projections with the Capital Model Actuary's refreshed BSCR runs under the planned actions.
Obtain board approval, then have Regulatory Counsel clear and the Principal Representative and CFO sign; file with the BMA within 45 days of the failure.
Track plan milestones weekly on the breach event until coverage restores.
checklist.done: a board-approved, BMA-filed remediation plan exists within 45 days with weekly milestone tracking running.

checklist.step: Coordinate MSM-level contingency readiness
actions: Maintain the contingency playbook for coverage approaching the Minimum Solvency Margin: the Act's consequences (restrictions on business, BMA directions under its intervention powers) and the company's pre-agreed response.
Verify annually that contingency funding options (parental support letters, committed facilities from the Treasury Manager) remain executable.
Test the playbook in the annual stress exercise using the CISSA scenarios.
Report readiness to the board Risk Committee annually.
checklist.done: an annually tested MSM contingency playbook with verified funding options is reported to the board.

checklist.step: Embed capital gates into dividend and transaction approvals
actions: Require a pre-transaction coverage check for every dividend, share buyback, large reinsurance commutation or affiliate loan: projected post-transaction coverage must clear the amber trigger.
Record each check with the transaction papers and the projected ladder position.
Block any transaction projecting coverage below amber pending CFO and, below TCL, board approval — mirroring the statutory constraints on capital distributions.
Reconcile executed transactions against the checks quarterly.
checklist.done: every capital transaction carries a pre-approval coverage check and none executed below the gate without the required approval.

checklist.step: Log monitoring exceptions with disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every late monthly estimate, missed escalation step, ladder misconfiguration or late notification, with root cause and owner.
Distinguish data causes (GL close late) from process causes (alert misrouted) — the fixes differ.
Review open exceptions at the monthly capital committee until closed.
Close only on evidence of the corrected estimate, alert or configuration.
checklist.done: every monitoring exception is tracked with root cause and closed on evidence at the capital committee.

checklist.step: Report the capital position to the board quarterly
actions: Deliver the quarterly capital adequacy report via the board portal: coverage against the full ladder, movement analysis, stress results, breach events and remediation status.
Include the reconciliation of monthly estimates to the quarterly BSCR refresh so the board sees estimation reliability.
Minute the board's challenge and directed actions.
File the report with the quarter's coverage pack.
checklist.done: quarterly board reporting covers the ladder position, estimation reliability and breach status with minutes filed.

checklist.step: Run the annual stress and scenario overlay
actions: Run the CISSA stress scenarios (cat events, market shocks, reserve deterioration, combined scenarios) against current coverage in the actuarial platform.
Identify the scenarios that breach amber, TCL and ECR, and the management actions each would demand.
Feed the results into the trigger-ladder recalibration and the contingency playbook test.
Present the stress results at the capital committee and to the board Risk Committee.
checklist.done: annual stresses identify breach-driving scenarios and feed the ladder recalibration and playbook, with results presented.

checklist.step: Archive the monitoring evidence continuously
actions: File monthly estimate workbooks, committee minutes, breach events, notifications and plans in the financial reporting repository under REG-057-C32 / <yyyy>.
Apply the 10-year retention label.
Run a quarterly retrieval check pulling one prior month's estimate and its committee minute.
Record the repository links on the capital calendar entries.
checklist.done: monitoring evidence is filed continuously with 10-year retention and passes quarterly retrieval checks.

testing.step: Build the population of estimates, packs and breach events
actions: Pull the year's twelve monthly estimate workbooks, four quarterly coverage packs and the GRC breach-event log from the financial reporting repository and GRC platform.
List every ad-hoc estimate triggered by watchlist events.
Record counts; a missing month or quarter is an immediate exception.
Fix the tested trigger-ladder version(s) in force during the year with their approval evidence.
testing.done: a complete inventory of estimates, packs, ad-hoc runs and breach events exists with ladder versions fixed.

testing.step: Verify monthly production timeliness
actions: Compare each monthly estimate's publication timestamp (dashboard or file metadata) to working day 10 of the following month.
Compare each quarterly refresh delivery to the 20-business-day standard.
Verify from metadata, not from cover-sheet dates.
List every late month with its day count against the 12-of-12 threshold.
testing.done: all estimate and refresh timings are verified from metadata against their standards.

testing.step: Recompute sampled monthly estimates
actions: Select 3 months with a recorded seed, including any month adjacent to a trigger breach.
Re-perform each roll-forward from the GL close data: opening eligible capital, net income, valuation movements, dividends and capital transactions.
Recompute coverage against the ECR denominator the procedure prescribed for that month and compare to the published figure.
Any difference beyond rounding is an exception with its ladder impact noted.
testing.done: three sampled months recompute from GL data to the published coverage with differences and ladder impacts listed.

testing.step: Verify the trigger ladder was correctly configured
actions: Read the dashboard's configured amber/red/ECR/MSM values for each period and compare to the approved procedure values and the filed BSCR figures (TCL = 120% × filed ECR).
Confirm the denominators reset when each quarterly refresh landed.
Recheck that the amber trigger sat above TCL throughout — a ladder inversion silently disables early warning.
List any misconfiguration with its duration.
testing.done: dashboard trigger values reconcile to approved figures for every period with misconfigurations timed.

testing.step: Independently detect breaches the monitoring should have caught
actions: Using the recomputed coverage series and the approved ladder, independently flag every month and ad-hoc point where coverage crossed amber, TCL, ECR or MSM.
Reconcile your flags to the GRC breach-event log; a crossing with no logged event is a monitoring-failure exception — the fail condition of this control.
Check watchlist events in the year (cat losses, market shocks) triggered the required ad-hoc estimates.
Document the comparison in the workpaper.
testing.done: every independently detected crossing matches a logged breach event, or monitoring failures are reported.

testing.step: Re-verify escalation timeliness for each breach event
actions: For each amber event, verify same-day logging and the written CFO/CRO notification within 2 business days from email timestamps.
For any TCL event, verify the board Risk Committee convened within 10 business days from the meeting record.
Verify weekly estimation actually ran during breach periods by counting the filed weekly workbooks.
List every blown escalation step with its actual timing.
testing.done: every breach event's escalation chain is verified step by step from timestamps.

testing.step: Recompute the 14-day and 45-day statutory clocks on any ECR failure
actions: For any ECR failure event, establish the awareness date from the earliest document showing sub-ECR coverage — not the date management recorded as awareness.
Recompute BMA notification date − awareness date against 14 days, and remediation plan filing date − failure date against 45 days, from delivery proofs.
Confirm the notification and plan carried counsel clearance and the Principal Representative's and CFO's signatures.
If no ECR failure occurred in the year, evidence that conclusion from the recomputed coverage series and mark the step not-applicable-with-evidence.
testing.done: statutory day counts recompute within 14 and 45 days from true awareness dates, or non-occurrence is positively evidenced.

testing.step: Test the transaction capital gates
actions: List the year's dividends, buybacks, commutations and affiliate loans from board minutes and the Treasury Manager's records.
For each, verify a pre-transaction coverage check exists, pre-dates execution and projected coverage above the gate.
Recompute one dividend's post-transaction coverage from the estimate workbook.
Any transaction without a pre-dated check, or executed below the gate without the required approval, is an exception.
testing.done: every capital transaction traces to a pre-dated passing coverage check or a documented required approval.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception, splitting computation errors, ladder misconfigurations, monitoring failures, escalation misses and gate bypasses.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date.
Route any missed statutory notification window to Regulatory Counsel for an immediate disclosure decision — this cannot wait for the report cycle.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception is tracked with owner and date, and missed statutory windows get an immediate counsel decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute results against the thresholds (12/12 timely estimates, zero undetected crossings, statutory clocks met) and write the conclusion with workpaper references.
Have the Chief Audit Executive, who produced no estimate and operated no escalation, review and sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit/Risk Committee with the quarterly capital adequacy report.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057-C32.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the committee.
